Stated Claim / Post Context:
Looksmaxxing influencer Clavicular pleads not guilty to charges that he raped a teenager in Massachusetts

'Looksmaxxing' influencer Braden Peters, a.k.a. Clavicular, has pleaded not guilty to charges that he raped a teenager at his family home.

Actual Article Body:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here.

See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search.   Set us as preferred

Clavicular, the manosphere influencer known for his looksmaxxing content, pleaded not guilty Thursday to charges that he raped a teenager at his family home in Massachusetts.

The controversial internet personality, whose real name is Braden Peters, is accused of giving a 17-year-old girl alcohol until she was drunk, then sexually assaulting her, in May 2025. In September, he was charged with one felony count of rape and one felony count for drugging someone for sexual intercourse. He is also charged with a misdemeanor count of providing alcohol to someone younger than 21.

Peters has denied the allegations through his lawyers and says the sexual encounter was consensual, according to the Associated Press.

Entertainment & Arts

Clavicular, the social media influencer known for his looksmaxxing content, faces two felony charges for drugging and rape.

Peters allegedly invited the teen to a home owned by his family in Chatham, on Cape Cod, and served her alcohol while livestreaming and had sex with her “several times” after the webcast ended, according to the New York Times. Police later concluded that she lacked the capacity to consent, based on her likely level of intoxication, per the outlet.

The 20-year-old social media star reportedly arrived on Thursday at the courthouse in Orleans, Mass.,  walking a dog that barked at reporters. Peters ignored reporters’ questions and spoke only to the dog as he entered the building.

Judge John Julian, who presided over the hearing, set bail at $10,000, which Peters posted immediately after. Peters also surrendered his passport and, as part of his bail conditions, agreed to refrain from contacting or posting about his accuser.

The case marks the latest legal challenge for Peters, whose internet notoriety crossed into the mainstream after previous brushes with the law. In March, he was charged with misdemeanor battery after police alleged he instigated a fight between two women and posted a video of it online. That charge was later dropped. In May, he was charged with a misdemeanor for unlawfully discharging a firearm in public in relation to a viral video that showed an alligator being repeatedly shot. After pleading no contest, he was sentenced to probation.

Entertainment & Arts

YouTube has once again removed the channels of controversial manosphere personality Clavicular. He was first kicked off the platform in November.

The woman accusing Peters of rape in this latest case also filed a civil lawsuit against him in April in Florida.

Peters rose to internet prominence as a proponent of looksmaxxing, a trend related to extreme measures to improve one’s physical appearance. Peters has acknowledged using hard drugs and smashing the bones of his face with a hammer to maximize his looks.

The term and so-called self-improvement practice are generally associated with the incel community, though Peters has previously taken offense to that. “Incel” is a term that generally refers to extremely online men whose “involuntary celibacy” has shaped their attitudes toward women and other worldviews.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Syrian who raped girl, 16, 'gang-raped another woman' after German police released him while probing earlier sex assault

Ahmad A., 26, was arrested after the first attack at an asylum accommodation centre in Munich, Bavaria, southern Germany, on February 27, 2025.

Actual Article Body:
By SABRINA PENTY, FOREIGN NEWS REPORTER

Published:  01:09 AEDT, 23 October 2026   |  Updated:  04:44 AEDT, 23 October 2026

A Syrian man who was being investigated over the rape of a 16-year-old girl allegedly sexually assaulted another woman just weeks after German police released him from custody.

Ahmad A., 26, was arrested after the first attack at an asylum accommodation centre in Munich, Bavaria, southern Germany, on February 27, 2025.

He was released on April 8, 2025 after prosecutors requested that his detention be suspended because the teenage victim could not be questioned due to her psychological state.

According to local media, the girl was twice unable to attend questioning before an investigating judge, despite her testimony being considered central to the case.

Munich public prosecutor Juliane Grotz explained the decision, saying: 'We submitted the application to suspend the arrest warrant because, given the circumstances described, we could no longer meet the requirement to expedite proceedings involving people in custody.'

After his release, Ahmad was required to report to police twice a week and was forbidden from approaching the teenage victim or a witness.

But on July 15, 2025, he allegedly attacked another woman alongside Haidar A., 31, and Mousa H., 27, both from Yemen.

The 29-year-old woman was near an underground station in Munich when she encountered Ahmad and asked him for a cigarette.

Ahmad A is accused of raping two women on separate occasions in the German city of Munich

According to the indictment, the three men later took her to an isolated staircase beneath the Wittelsbacher Bridge over the River Isar.

Ahmad allegedly grabbed the woman and dragged her down the stairs as she screamed and repeatedly shouted 'no' in English.

All three are accused of taking turns to rape the woman.

After the alleged assault, the men reportedly walked back towards a petrol station with the woman.

When she spotted a group of people, she threw a water bottle to the ground to distract the men before running towards the group.

The three suspects fled, and police arrested them in September 2025.

The case is now being heard at Munich I Regional Court, where Ahmad's lawyer, Michael Weiss, has disputed the prosecution's account.

Speaking to local media, he said: 'According to my client, everything was consensual.'

The trial is scheduled to continue on October 27.

Ahmad has already been convicted in the earlier case involving the teenage girl. In November 2025, a district court sentenced him to two years and six months in prison.

He faces the prospect of further imprisonment if convicted in the second case.

The circumstances surrounding his release have raised questions about why the proceedings involving the teenage victim could not progress quickly enough to maintain his pre-trial detention.

The second case remains ongoing.
